units.title: The selected spherical numerator
units.reader_note: Exact source range and actual measures; assumptions, proof and exact Lean are folded below.
units.statement: The two normalized surface moments evaluate the selected numerator.
assumptions: Exactly \(n\in\mathbb N,\ n\ge3\) and \(\kappa\in\mathbb R,\ \kappa\ge4\), including equality. No parity restriction is imposed; \(n/2\) is real even when n is odd.

The selected parameters imply \(s\ge2\), \(0<r<1\), \(\ell>0\) and \(1-r^2>0\). These domain facts and every needed L1/measure identity are proved inside existing canonical dependencies, never supplied as extra assumptions.
All expectations are actual real Bochner integrals. Absolute integrability is a conclusion. Standard totalized division/rpow off the measure support changes none of the asserted integrals.
\(\sigma\) is the actual normalized ambient surface law defined below. The A1 input is used only in the unambiguous source range \(n\ge3\).

notation.text: All divisions and n/2 exponents here are real; n−1 is natural subtraction in prefactors.

The first source coordinate is Lean coordinate 0. The ambient measure is the inclusion pushforward of the normalized volume-derived unit-sphere measure. The kernel is defined on all Euclidean space with standard totalized real division and Real.rpow, and integrated only under sigma.

steps.title: Use both actual normalized surface moments
steps.text: The selected-parameter theorem proves the strict radial domain. Apply the canonical A1 moment node at that r; it supplies both absolute integrability statements and both actual values.
steps.lean: ht calls SelectedTilt.selected_tilt; hm calls SphericalPoisson.spherical_poisson_moments with n≥2 deduced from hn. The paper use stays n≥3.

steps.title: Form the integrable linear combination
steps.text: Split the unchanged numerator over the same denominator. Both coefficients are finite real constants, so genuine L1 is preserved.
steps.lean: heq is the pointwise equality; hf consumes the two moment Integrable conclusions by const_mul and sub.

steps.title: Evaluate and cancel the selected parameter
steps.text: Linearity gives the first fraction. Substitute the literal r and cancel only nonzero n and s+1, derived from the source range.
steps.lean: hnum proves (s+1)r−(s−1)=−(s−1)/n. integral_sub and integral_const_mul consume the L1 facts; hm supplies both values. This is the same declaration/proof previously in Tests/GaussianComplexitySphericalPoisson.lean.

units.title: Eq24: the evaluated signed Gaussian expectation
units.reader_note: Exact source range and actual measures; assumptions, proof and exact Lean are folded below.
units.statement: The actual Gaussian and density expectations have the same exact value.
assumptions: Exactly \(n\in\mathbb N,\ n\ge3\) and \(\kappa\in\mathbb R,\ \kappa\ge4\), including equality. No parity restriction is imposed; \(n/2\) is real even when n is odd.

The selected parameters imply \(s\ge2\), \(0<r<1\), \(\ell>0\) and \(1-r^2>0\). These domain facts and every needed L1/measure identity are proved inside existing canonical dependencies, never supplied as extra assumptions.
All expectations are actual real Bochner integrals. Absolute integrability is a conclusion. Standard totalized division/rpow off the measure support changes none of the asserted integrals.

Both outer integrands \(O\mapsto\det(O)\int t\,d\gamma_O\) and \(O\mapsto\det(O)\int t p_O\,dx\) are in \(L^1(\mu)\). These facts, the density identity and positive definiteness are internally supplied conclusions, not extra binders.

notation.text: All divisions and n/2 exponents here are real; n−1 is natural subtraction in prefactors.

Mu is normalized Haar on the full real orthogonal group including both determinant signs. A is precision; its inverse is covariance of the actual multivariateGaussian. The density uses Euclidean Lebesgue measure, the Euclidean dot product and the actual l2 norm.

The first source coordinate is Lean coordinate 0. The ambient measure is the inclusion pushforward of the normalized volume-derived unit-sphere measure. The kernel is defined on all Euclidean space with standard totalized real division and Real.rpow, and integrated only under sigma.

steps.title: Attach the actual Gaussian to the normalized sphere
steps.text: Use the already compiled selected Gaussian surface transport. Its normalized sphere is exactly the one used by the numerator theorem.
steps.lean: hs consumes SurfaceLaw.selected_surface_transport hn hκ. Its Gaussian is the actual law with inverse precision as covariance; its sphere is literal normalized volume.toSphere.

steps.title: Insert the two-moment numerator value
steps.text: Use the single existing numerator node; do not reproduce either A1 proof or assume a moment value.
steps.lean: hm is selected_numerator_value hn hκ; rw [hm] at hs replaces the actual surface integral. The global declaration was promoted byte-for-byte to SelectedNumerator.lean.

steps.title: Collect signs and powers
steps.text: Because n≥3, n=(n−1)+1. The extra minus sign and factor s−1 raise both natural powers by one. Keep the real dimension-half power unchanged.
steps.lean: hpow uses Nat.sub_add_cancel and pow_succ. div_pow and field_simp combine the exact factors. hn0, hsp and hden justify the nonzero denominators.

steps.title: Transfer the value and L1 to the literal density integral
steps.text: The canonical actual-Gaussian theorem supplies signed outer L1 and pointwise equality between each Gaussian expectation and its Euclidean density integral. Multiplication by the determinant preserves equality, so both outer integrands have the same L1 and integral.
steps.lean: hg is GaussianExpectation.actual_gaussian_transform at the internally positive selected tilt. hpoint is the everywhere equality promoted to AE; Integrable.congr and integral_congr_ae transfer L1 and the value. Both are conclusions of the sealed theorem.

steps.title: Consume the value in the actual target mixtures
steps.text: For ν±=2μ restricted to determinant ±1, the real Gaussian mixtures P±=ν± bind γ have integrable test t. The canonical gap theorem and Eq24 give the ordered gap, with its factor two. Strict parameter domains prove v≠0.
steps.lean: Tests/GaussianComplexityEvaluatedGaussian.lean calls MixtureExpectation.actual_mixture_expectation_gap and this theorem. Nonzero follows from n>0, s≥2, the positive base 1−1/n, and 1−r²>0. This consumer does not assert a quantitative TV or query lower bound.
